correctness.rationale: For regular n>=5 polygon circumradius R and edge unit tangents t_j, perpendicular projection onto edge j lies in the segment precisely when |y·t_j|<=s=R sin(pi/n). Strict satisfaction yields a normal from each of n edges and each of n vertices; no face can give >1 normal by base point, so maximal generic count 2n. The closed simultaneous strip intersection S_n is contained in P_n because its circumradius is R sin x/cos(x/2) (odd) or R tan x (even), each <= R cos x for stipulated ranges. Directions mod sign yield regular 2n-gon (odd) or n-gon (even), with inradius s. Computing area (perimeter*inradius/2) yields 2 tan x tan(x/2) or tan² x, with Taylor coefficients 5/12 and 2/3 at x^4. Independently reconstructed clipping intersections and area ratios for 12 orders 5..30. Chamber boundaries measure zero and are not claimed to have exactly 2n distinct normals.

evidence: General 2024 theorem bounds normals by total number of faces and characterizes active regions, but does not state the exact area of their joint intersection for every regular polygon. Published odd-regular average formula concerns mean number, not maximal chamber.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A general upper bound on count 2n cannot imply the measure or side count of the maximizer locus. New calculation specializes to regular Euclidean n>=5 and provides the missing quantitative geometry.
